builder_plan.scenario: Your coding assistant makes changes that still need substantial repair before merging.
builder_plan.change: Try the technique on held-out issues from a repository with reliable tests.
builder_plan.baseline: The same coding agent, repository snapshot, tools, and token budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct patches, regression failures, human repair time, and total cost per accepted change.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: (When) Should a Software Factory be Lights-off? Benchmarking Code Review Agents on Bug Detection
summary: The method replaces human-first-pass code review on agent-generated pull requests with an LLM review agent, optionally steered by exploration-nudging prompts and supplied repository context. Cost is per-PR API inference (about 10% more for the improved prompting) plus pipeline work to supply project knowledge and to scale review effort with PR complexity. Detection degrades on complex changes, on bugs requiring non-local reasoning, and sharply on proprietary code where project context is missing, so fully lights-off review would silently pass bugs.
rationale: The paper provides directly actionable guidance for API-only teams: adopt review agents as a bug-catching layer with complexity-scaled effort and repository context, while retaining human review for complex or context-heavy PRs.

claims.statement: The method replaces human-first-pass code review on agent-generated pull requests with an LLM review agent, optionally steered by exploration-nudging prompts and supplied repository context. Cost is per-PR API inference (about 10% more for the improved prompting) plus pipeline work to supply project knowledge and to scale review effort with PR complexity. Detection degrades on complex changes, on bugs requiring non-local reasoning, and sharply on proprietary code where project context is missing, so fully lights-off review would silently pass bugs.

Best review agent (claude-opus-5 with copilot-cli) detects 71.9% of human-verified bugs within its top-5 comments; exploration-nudging prompts add up to 5.8 percentage points at roughly 10% higher cost.
